'''Eden Detention Center''' is a privately owned and operated prison for men located in [[Eden, Texas]], United States. Run by the [[Corrections Corporation of America]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Eden Detention Center |url=http://www.cca.com/facilities/eden-detention-center |website=Corrections Corporation of America |access-date=20 August 2016 |archive-date=29 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160829135951/http://www.cca.com/facilities/eden-detention-center |url-status=live }}</ref> the low-security facility was established in 1985 under a contract with the [[Federal Bureau of Prisons]] (FBOP). A large percentage of inmates are composed of illegal migrants from Mexico and other Latin American countries.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=5 March 1995 |title=Eden Detention Center to add more housing |language=en |page=5 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789384596 |url-access=subscription |accessdate=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612021113/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789384596 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== History ==
Initially, the creation of a privately run prison was seen as a benefit to the town of Eden, bringing in job opportunities and growth. Upon its opening in 1985, it employed 27 people, or 2% of the town's population.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Daniel |first=Carol |date=2 February 1986 |title=Center brings benefits to Eden |language=en |page=1C |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788454837 |url-access=subscription |accessdate=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611192901/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788454837 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Renovations to the prison were made to the center in 1988 to make up for structural insecurities discovered from the initial construction, which lacked appropriate oversight to ensure safety of prisoners.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=McSwain |first=Ross |date=19 June 1988 |title=Prison safety |language=en |page=1 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788561432 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611194223/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788561432 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 1 December 1988, many prisoners from EDC were temporarily transferred to other federal prisons following a fire that broke out in the attic of the center, causing damage to certain parts of the facility. No injuries were reported.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2 December 1988 |title=Fire at Eden Federal Prison sends its inmates to others |language=en |page=4 |work=[[Tyler Morning Telegraph|The Tyler Courier-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/589266678 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611194221/https://www.newspapers.com/image/589266678 |url-status=live }}</ref> An open house was held in January 1989 to showcase renovations made to the public following the blaze.<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 December 1988 |title=Detention center sets open house |language=en |page=18 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789074901 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611195331/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789074901 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In response to growing need for more space and the success of the privately owned model, EDC began its first expansion in 1990.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Amos |first=Kathy |date=31 December 1989 |title=Eden |language=en |page=14C |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788741306 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=13 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230613181601/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788741306 |url-status=live }}</ref> A second expansion came in the form of added housing and recreation in 1995 following the expectation that the center would increase its population by 296, to a total of 950 inmates.<ref name=":0" /> The dormitory ended up seeing actual capacity raised to 1,006.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tait |first=Grant |date=16 August 1995 |title=Eden center opens door to new wing |language=en |page=15 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789575010 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612020933/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789575010 |url-status=live }}</ref>

A 1993 agreement between Attorney General [[Janet Reno]] and Mexican Attorney General [[Jorge Carpizo McGregor|Jorge Carpizo]] based on the [[Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965|Immigration and Nationality Act]] (INA) reduced the overall prison population after agreeing to deport non-naturalized criminals back to Mexico to serve out their sentence. Prisons like EDC were specifically affected due to their high Hispanic populations.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=Andy |date=15 October 1993 |title=Project may cut facility's inmates |language=en |page=1 |work=[[San Angelo Standard Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789484715 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612021053/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789484715 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In October 1995, owner Roy Burnes, who had owned the prison since its creation, sold the EDC to [[Corrections corporation of america|Corrections Corporation of America]] (now CoreCivic) for $18,000,000.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Durhama |first=Ron |date=5 October 1995 |title=Owner sells Eden Detention Center |language=en |page=10A |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789498766 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612021112/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789498766 |url-status=live }}</ref> During the transition, Larry Craven was named interim warden, and Dolan Waller was named assistant warden.<ref>{{Cite news |date=12 November 1995 |title=CCA names Eden center wardens |language=en |page=2 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789571663 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612021437/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789571663 |url-status=live }}</ref>

CCA sold the center to Prison Realty Corp. in 1999 for $28,000,000.<ref>{{Cite news |date=16 March 1999 |title=Prison Realty to buy Texas town's facility |language=en |page=D35 |work=[[The Kansas City Star]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/685554962/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=12 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612120056/https://www.newspapers.com/image/685554962/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Within the same year, Prison Realty Corp. merged with CCA.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CCA – Prison Realty Merger Approved |work=Prison Legal News |url=https://www.prisonlegalnews.org/news/1999/jun/15/cca-prison-realty-merger-approved/ |accessdate=12 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612120057/https://www.prisonlegalnews.org/news/1999/jun/15/cca-prison-realty-merger-approved/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In August 2016, [[United States Department of Justice|Department of Justice]] officials reported that the FBOP would be reducing its use of contracted facilities, on the grounds that private prisons provided less effective and less safe services with no major cost reductions. The agency expects to permit current contracts on its thirteen remaining private facilities to expire.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Zapotosky |first1=Matt |date=18 August 2016 |title=Justice Department says it will end use of private prisons |newspaper=Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/post-nation/wp/2016/08/18/justice-department-says-it-will-end-use-of-private-prisons/ |access-date=19 August 2016 |archive-date=19 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819065941/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/post-nation/wp/2016/08/18/justice-department-says-it-will-end-use-of-private-prisons/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The facility was shut down in 2017 when the contract with the FBOP was terminated. In 2019, the facility was reopened under a different contract with the [[U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] for 660 beds and the [[United States Marshals Service]] for 844 beds.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Edgin |first1=Alana |title=Eden Detention Center to reopen with government contract two years after closing |url=https://www.gosanangelo.com/story/news/local/2019/05/23/eden-texas-detention-center-reopen-ice-u-s-marshals-contract/1204626001/ |website=gosanangelo.com |access-date=2 August 2019 |archive-date=2 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802113446/https://www.gosanangelo.com/story/news/local/2019/05/23/eden-texas-detention-center-reopen-ice-u-s-marshals-contract/1204626001/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Prisoner protests ===
Throughout the history of Eden Detention Center, there have been several protests, petitions, and riots by prisoners against alleged substandard living conditions and lack of wanted privileges.

==== Petition protest ====
In June 1987, 111 prisoners detained in the center (67.6% of all inmates) signed a letter complaining of civil rights violations and violations of prison standards, including: overcrowding beyond capacity, poor sanitation standards, and cost-cutting necessities for profit, such as denying prisoners changes of clothes or any underwear at all. Center president Roy Burnes denied the allegations, and [[San Antonio]] federal inspector John Morris stated that some of the complaints were overexaggerated.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Tomas |first=Jan |date=7 July 1987 |title=Eden prisoners say civil rights being violated |language=en |page=1 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788279739/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611192900/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788279739/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Further research by locals of the town concerned with the complaints agreed with federal investigations that prisoners had heavily embellished issues with the prison.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Murray |first=Nancy |date=14 July 1987 |title=Inmates at Eden shouldn't gripe |language=en |page=6 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788282632 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611194222/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788282632 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Mexican cuisine protest ====
During the evening of 23 May 1989, a formal protest was held where over 300 prisoners at the facility refused to return to their cells, citing substandard living conditions and unacceptable food quality. 12 law enforcement agencies deployed officers to deal with the situation.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |date=24 May 1989 |title=300 prisoners protest in Texas |language=en |page=6 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/572976769 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611195331/https://www.newspapers.com/image/572976769 |url-status=live }}</ref> Several mattresses were burned by prisoners, but no injuries were reported on either side.<ref>{{Cite news |date=24 May 1989 |title=EDEN, Texas – Disturbance |language=en |page=8 |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/229952055 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611195332/https://www.newspapers.com/image/229952055 |url-status=live }}</ref> An agreement was reached between four inmates, two representatives from the [[Federal Bureau of Prisons]], and two representatives from the prison administration to supply better quality food (specifically, [[Mexican cuisine]]) and to provide Spanish reading materials to Hispanic inmates, who composed 95% of all incarcerated people at the prison. Greg Bogdan of the FBP stated that the negotiation was the first of its kind between inmates and the department.<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 May 1989 |title=Uprising Ends Peacefully |language=en |page=10 (sec 4) |work=[[Tyler Morning Telegraph]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/587810961 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611200706/https://www.newspapers.com/image/587810961 |url-status=live }}</ref> The protest in total lasted over 20 hours.<ref>{{Cite news |date=27 May 1989 |title=Sheriff explains confusion in Eden |language=en |page=1 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788591860 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611200707/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788591860 |url-status=live }}</ref> Some speculate that the unusually high temperatures that week (with a maximum recorded temperature of 107 F) aggravated the prisoners beyond normal grievances.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=Rick |date=12 May 2000 |title=May's heat is nothing new in West Texas |language=en |pages=1A, 4A |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789641659 |url-access=subscription |access-date=12 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612121146/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789641659 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Recreation time protest ====
A similar protest to the May 1989 staging occurred on 29 October 1989, only 5 months after the previous one. A protest was held by 284 prisoners in the same manner in demand of more recreational privileges, sparked by a change in prisoner schedules.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Macias |first=Loretta |date=30 October 1989 |title=Second protest in six months hits Eden center |language=en |page=1 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788614380 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611204338/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788614380 |url-status=live }}</ref> Unlike the previous protest, negotiations "fell through", and prisoners proceeded to riot, smashing windows, setting off fire extinguishers, and breaking cameras and furniture, costing thousands of dollars in damages. Police forces arrived in [[riot gear]] and confined prisoners to the courtyard.<ref>{{Cite news |date=31 October 1989 |title=280 Inmates Riot; Time Change Cut Recreation |language=en |page=3 |work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/613329561 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611204340/https://www.newspapers.com/image/613329561 |url-status=live }}</ref> Following the disturbance, Ron Smith retired from position of prison superintendent, and was replaced by James T Kimberling, a former employee of the Federal Bureau of Prisons.<ref>{{Cite news |date=18 November 1989 |title=Eden prison superintendent named |language=en |page=1C |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788784408 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612095645/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788784408 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Vegetable protest ====
A fourth protest occurred on 6 March 1991 when three quarters of the 479 inmates refused to return to their quarters, although they did not initially set any demands, to the confusion of many administrators.<ref name=":5">{{Cite news |date=7 March 1991 |title=Inmates at Eden Detention Center refuse to go to quarters |language=en |page=9 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788634197 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611205245/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788634197 |url-status=live }}</ref> After taking over the food service area, many began engaging in [[Food fight|food fights]] and started small fires.<ref>{{Cite news |date=7 March 1991 |title=Inmates negotiate in Texas |language=en |page=3 |work=[[Spokane Daily Chronicle|Spokane Chronicle]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/567297807 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611205244/https://www.newspapers.com/image/567297807 |url-status=live }}</ref> Demands were eventually released by prisoners, requesting more vegetables for prison meals. They allegedly held off authorities with baseball bats and kitchen utensils.<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 May 1991 |title=News of the weird |language=en |page=2 |work=Greenfield Daily Times |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/904454926 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612010330/https://www.newspapers.com/image/904454926 |url-status=live }}</ref> The riot caused an estimated $250,000 in damages and one inmate was hospitalized after suffering a heart attack.<ref>{{Cite news |date=8 March 1991 |title=Eden inmates stage rebellion over vegetables |language=en |page=7 |work=[[Abilene Reporter-News]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/765047598 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611205243/https://www.newspapers.com/image/765047598 |url-status=live }}</ref> Unpopular locally, many residents of Eden and the surrounding areas felt that the FBI and prison superintendent caving to protestors was done in poor taste.<ref>{{Cite news |last=J.B. |first= |date=12 March 1991 |title=I'll tell you how I'd deal with the inmates at EDC |language=en |page=7 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788635336 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612010333/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788635336 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=No initials |date=13 March 1991 |title=This concerns the Eden detention center |language=en |page=7 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788635430 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612010333/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788635430 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Mexican cuisine protest II ====
A 5th protest nearly broke out when six inmates attempted to organize another one regarding food issues and medical care, acting up around 2:30 PM on 31 July 1991. They were quickly confined to separate quarters from the rest of the inmates. They were allegedly upset about the change in dinner for the evening, which consisted of chicken fried steak, rather than the Mexican food that was established following the May 1989 protest. Warden Jim Kimberling stated that the situation was defused once the old menu was brought back.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Becknell |first=Bob |date=1 August 1991 |title=Menu causes protest in Eden |language=en |page=1C |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788955602 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612010332/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788955602 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Food order protest ====
26 June 1992 saw a sixth protest (turned riot) by prisoners, who were dissatisfied with the order in which food was served that evening. Setting fire to the recreation center and library, the protesting inmates destroyed the roof of the building and many contents surrounding it. Rocks were also used as [[Catapult|trajectory weapons]]. The protest was quelled through a negotiation with prison staff who agreed to implement a new serving system by July and agreed to allow prisoners to receive [[Pornography|X-rated materials]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Becknell |first=Bob |date=28 June 1992 |title=Prison uprising – Authorities quell disturbance at Eden Detention Center |language=en |page=1 |work=[[San Angelo Standard Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788946876 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612011346/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788946876 |url-status=live }}</ref>

An aftershock of the protest continued two days later, leading to administrator John Morris requesting "30 to 35 ringleaders" be split up in various other federal prisons.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Coghlan |first=Keely |date=29 June 1992 |title=Eden Center still uneasy |language=en |page=1 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788947345 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612011348/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788947345 |url-status=live }}</ref> Morris sent a total of 54 people who were behind the uprising to various county jails throughout Texas, and claimed "that [they] won't be as comfortable as what we have here at E.D.C.", citing that although they consistently participated in protests against conditions, that the dormitories at EDC were fully stocked with televisions and microwave ovens.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Miller |first=Bill |date=30 June 1992 |title=Eden Detention Center sends 54 'ringleaders' to county jails |language=en |page=1 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788947701 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612021053/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788947701 |url-status=live }}</ref> It was later revealed that the second round of protesting occurred after several inmates were upset that there had not gotten adequate news coverage of the incident.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Land |first=Keith |date=1 July 1992 |title=Prisoners transferred after disturbances |language=en |page=A23 |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/643125639 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612021056/https://www.newspapers.com/image/643125639 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Reeves transfers ====
In a turn of events, May 1994 saw EDC receive 20 prisoners from the [[Reeves County Detention Complex]] following a protest at the Reeves facility that saw prisoners burning mattresses in protest of quarters inspections by guards. The protests occurred on 18 and 19 May, and prisoners were transferred following 20 May.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Stephens |first1=Dean |last2=Lister |first2=Karen |date=20 May 1994 |title=Reeves County prisoners burn mattresses in protest |language=en |page=13 |work=[[Odessa American]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/300782141 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612021113/https://www.newspapers.com/image/300782141 |url-status=live }}</ref>

A second incident in August 1994 saw six more inmates transferred to EDC from Reeves after riots sparked from corporate downsizing that resulted in the destruction of big screen TVs, exercise equipment, soda dispensers, and foosball tables. They also complained of 'salty water'.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McCracken |first=Peggy |date=30 August 1994 |title=Complaints spark inmates' rampage |language=en |pages=A1–A2 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/788814912/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612021109/https://www.newspapers.com/image/788814912/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== SWAT standoff ====
21 August 1995 saw the most violent standoff during a protest yet. Rather than negotiate similar to previous protests, the administration took up to calling [[SWAT]] teams who [[Tear gas|teargassed]] the building. The EDC warehouse was used as a triage to treat injuries from either side and [[U.S. Route 87 in Texas|Route 87]] was clogged with emergency response vehicles attempting to reach the center to treat injuries.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Hargrave |first1=Kacee |last2=Dial |first2=Marla |last3=Stanford |first3=Scott |last4=Irvin |first4=Mike |last5=Miller |first5=Bill |date=22 August 1996 |title=Uprising turns Eden into armed camp |language=en |page=4 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789360700 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612102338/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789360700 |url-status=live }}</ref> The protest began at 11:00 AM and continued well into the next day.<ref>{{Cite news |date=22 August 1996 |title=Order restored in Texas prison |language=en |page=3 |work=Sentinel Tribune |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/922261581 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612102849/https://www.newspapers.com/image/922261581 |url-status=live }}</ref> Although no demands were made prior to the riot, Craven stated that prisoners were unhappy with food service, hobby and crafts, and dental care.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hargrave |first=Kacee |date=22 August 1996 |title=Eden inmates riot: Prisoners take over recreation yard |language=en |page=1 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789360849 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612102334/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789360849 |url-status=live }}</ref> It was estimated that 400 of the 910 inmates participated in the riot.<ref name=":6">{{Cite news |date=22 August 1996 |title=Texas prisoners stage riot |language=en |page=6 |work=[[The Marshall News Messenger]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/331432203 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612102338/https://www.newspapers.com/image/331432203 |url-status=live }}</ref> At least thirteen inmates, two SWAT team members, and one warden were injured, with eight being hospitalized.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hargrave |first=Kacee |date=22 August 1996 |title=Inmates surrender after daylong sit-in |language=en |page=1 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789360690 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612102859/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789360690 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Following the riot, over 120 incarcerated undocumented immigrants who allegedly started the riot were transferred to other federal prisons, and were waiting for deportation.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hargrave |first=Kacee |date=23 August 1996 |title=Eden ships out inmates: Scores of aliens sent to other prisons after uprising |language=en |page=1 |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789360888 |url-access=subscription |access-date=12 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612114828/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789360888 |url-status=live }}</ref> Damages to the facility were declared minimal, as most of the fighting took place outside of the complex.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Shuler |first=Joel |date=24 August 1996 |title=Owner assesses riot's damage |language=en |page=1B |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789361127 |url-access=subscription |access-date=11 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612182447/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789361127 |url-status=live }}</ref> Four inmates, Enrique Perez-Munoz, Gilberto Garcia-Lua, Juan Balenzuela-Galaviz, and Ramon Inzunza-Sandoval, were all formally charged with [[Aggravated Assault|aggravated assault with a deadly weapon]] as a result of their actions during the riots. Prior to the riot, they had stockpiled over 16,000 pounds of rocks and had thrown multiple thousands of them during the altercation with SWAT. Following the riot, a select number of inmates alleged that they had been abused by prison guards, including being [[Sodomy|sodomized]] with [[Baton (law enforcement)|night sticks]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hargrave |first=Kacee |date=1 September 1996 |title=Eden inmates charged; beatings claimed |language=en |pages=A1–A2 |work=[[San Angelo Standard Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/789490683 |url-access=subscription |access-date=12 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612114829/https://www.newspapers.com/image/789490683 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Gang riots ====
After over five years of tranquility, another riot took place in the prison on 13 March 2001 when members from two rival gang groups butted heads. One inmate was hospitalized with a [[laceration]] to the head.<ref>{{Cite news |date=15 March 2001 |title=Rioting leaves one injuried |language=en |page=4A |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/790966597 |url-access=subscription |access-date=12 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612121142/https://www.newspapers.com/image/790966597 |url-status=live }}</ref> Two inmates, Juan Maldonado-Hernandez and Miguel Martinez-Lopez, were found guily of assaulting guard Tommy Jackson during the riot.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Williams Perner |first=Melissa Lynn |date=8 August 2001 |title=Eden prison inmates found guilty for assaulting guard during riot |language=en |page=2A |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/790965074 |url-access=subscription |access-date=12 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612123603/https://www.newspapers.com/image/790965074 |url-status=live }}</ref> On top of their then-current sentences, a judge added 10 years to their incarceration for the assault.<ref>{{Cite news |date=8 January 2002 |title=3 prisoners extend jail time for assault |language=en |page=4A |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/791059180 |url-access=subscription |access-date=12 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612125315/https://www.newspapers.com/image/791059180 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Another fight following on 1 May 2003 where a 30-minute fight ensued, causing 11 prisoners to be sent to the hospital for injuries.<ref>{{Cite news |date=3 May 2003 |title=West Texas center locked down after inmates fight |language=en |page=9A |work=[[The Victoria Advocate]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/434533320 |url-access=subscription |access-date=12 June 2023 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612123231/https://www.newspapers.com/image/434533320 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Dormitory B riots ====
Another riot occurred nearly seven years later on 12 April 2010 after the prisoners of Dormitory B refused to return to their cells. An overnight riot took place, and law enforcement was summoned and used 'chemical agents' to enforce compliance among the prisoners. No major injuries were reported.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Waller |first=Matthew |date=13 April 2010 |title=Eden Detention Center locked down after riot |language=en |page=3A |work=[[San Angelo Standard-Times]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/779938828 |url-access=subscription |access-date=12 June 2023 |archive-date=13 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230613122535/https://www.newspapers.com/image/779938828 |url-status=live }}</ref>
